sources.articleTitle: Why PG doctors are quitting premier medical institutes
Telangana gets 359 additional PG medical seats in government colleges for 2026-27, intake rises to 1,625

headline: Telangana Expands Medical Seats Amid Broader Faculty Departures
seoTitle: Telangana Increases Medical Intake Amid Staffing Issues
metaDescription: Telangana adds 359 postgraduate medical seats in public colleges, while reports suggest rising staff exits at major national medical institutes.
aiSummaryBullets: Telangana increased its postgraduate medical seat count by 359 across state-run institutions for the 2026-27 academic year.
The expansion brings the total state government medical intake to 1,625 seats across 23 colleges.
Data indicates an increase in postgraduate medical staff departures across various premier national institutes.
aiContextParagraph: Government authorities in Telangana have announced a significant expansion in medical education infrastructure, adding 359 new postgraduate seats to public medical colleges for the upcoming 2026-27 academic cycle. This development increases the total capacity to 1,625 seats and expands postgraduate offerings to 23 of the state's 35 government-run medical institutions. Concurrently, reports based on official responses to public information requests suggest a trend of postgraduate medical professionals leaving prominent national institutes. These departures have been documented across multiple campuses, including several AIIMS locations and JIPMER. While some individual institutions have observed shifts in these numbers, the availability of comprehensive, consolidated national data regarding staff resignation trends, workplace environment factors, and counselling services remains limited. The interplay between capacity expansion in state facilities and personnel turnover at central institutes marks a period of change in India's medical training sector.
whyItIsViral: The topic is gaining moderate traction due to the dual focus on significant state-level education expansion and recurring staff retention issues at national medical hubs.
